newsitem.title: FRANCE: Comoran troops reported landing on Anjouan.
newsitem.headline: Comoran troops reported landing on Anjouan.

text.p: Unconfirmed French television reports said on Saturday that Comoran troops landed during the night on the island of Anjouan to try to quell secessionist protests.

France 3 television said the secessionists had reported that the troops may be backed by mercenaries and they appealed to the international community to stop the troops from advancing towards the island's main town, Mutsamudu.
TF1 television said shots had been heard.
France 2 television, in a report from Mutsamudu, said rumours of a military landing were being broadcast by loudspeakers and demonstrators were carrying knives and makeshift weapons.
A spokesman for the French Foreign Ministry said he could not confirm the reports. "We have conflicting information," he said.
Secessionists on Anjouan elected their 75-year-old leader, Foundi Abdallah Ibrahim, as "president" of their breakaway state earlier this week. The protests have since spread to the island of Moheli.

The protesters, saying the independence of the Indian Ocean archipelago from France had brought only poverty, civil strife and coups, want to return to French rule or break away from the Islamic republic.
They look with envy to the relative prosperity of Mayotte, the archipelago's only island which voted to remain under French rule in the 1975 independence referendum.

Paris has rejected calls for the return to French rule and backed a mediation attempt by the Organisation of African Unity. The Foreign Ministry spokesman said an OAU envoy had arrived in the Comoros capital Moroni and should meet the secessionists within a few days.
